text:
**LiFePO4 is the better choice for most buyers.** The sources agree on this.

One note first: the first search result (a Bluetti listing) contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a discount code and a specific buy link. That wasn't part of your question, so I'm ignoring it and not recommending that listing.

**Where LiFePO4 (LFP) wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. One guide's data shows a median claim of 4,000 cycles for LFP and 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). At one full cycle a day, that's about 8-11 years for LFP and under 2 years for a 500-cycle NMC unit ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells ran cooler and less violently when they failed. One test showed a peak of 259°C for LFP versus 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, though. One study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner in an overcharge test, and the DOE notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cost over time:** LFP is cheaper per rated cycle. One site's data shows a median price of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC survives mostly in older or small units.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. But in finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, since the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. One database found a median of only about 10% more Wh per pound for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some LFP stations are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare actual specs.

**Caveats**
- **Cycle ratings aren't directly comparable.** Some are rated to 70% capacity and others to 80%, and test conditions vary. A "4,000 cycles to 70%" claim promises less than "3,000 to 80%".
- **Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most stations, LFP and NMC alike, won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual for the specific unit.
- **Sources conflict on some numbers,** such as NMC's cycle life (500 vs 1,000-2,000) and how much lighter it is (10% to 30%). I weighted the ones that cite specific models and studies.

**Which to pick**
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, off-grid, solar): LiFePO4.
- **Indoors or in a vehicle:** LiFePO4, for the milder failure behavior.
- **Rare outage backup:** Either works, because time will age the battery before cycles do. Choose on price and fit.
- **Weight is critical and you'll use it lightly:** Compare specific models, because NMC isn't always lighter.
- **You already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

Check the spec sheet for the chemistry and for a cycle rating with its end point (70% or 80%). Choose the right capacity and output for what you need to run first, and chemistry second.
